surface_summary: James Cunningham, Sr. is found murdered in his apartment, tied to a chair and shot. Suspicion falls on several family members and associates, including his nephews and a land agent, with conflicting testimonies and secret marriages complicating the case.
accepted_facts: James Cunningham, Sr. was found dead with a bullet wound to the head
He was tied to a chair and chloroformed before being shot
Several people were seen entering or leaving the apartment around the time of the murder
A large sum of money was withdrawn from the bank the day of the murder and went missing
inferred_conclusions: Kirby Lane was the murderer because he was seen entering and leaving the apartment
Cass Hull killed James Cunningham in a fit of rage during a dispute
James Cunningham, Jr. killed his uncle to inherit the fortune
mechanism_description: Shibo Horikawa, the Japanese valet, killed James Cunningham, Sr. by chloroforming him, tying him to a chair, and then shooting him at close range. He also killed Horikawa to silence him. Shibo acted out of self-preservation after Cunningham discovered his plan to steal money and frame others.
delivery_path: Shibo chloroformed James Cunningham, Sr. and tied him to a chair
Shibo shot Cunningham at close range with an automatic pistol
Shibo and Horikawa fled through the window to the fire escape
Horikawa hid in a neighboring apartment, supplied with newspapers and food by Shibo
Shibo killed Horikawa to prevent him from revealing the truth
Shibo attempted to murder Kirby Lane to prevent exposure
Shibo was captured and confessed to the murders
outcome_result: Shibo Horikawa is arrested and confesses to the murders of James Cunningham, Sr. and Horikawa.

false_assumption.statement: Wild Rose McLean was the murderer because her glove was found at the crime scene.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The glove with a rose embroidery was found at the scene, and Wild Rose was known to be present in the apartment shortly before the murder. Her passionate anger towards James Cunningham also provided a plausible motive.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: The glove was left inadvertently and taken by Kirby Lane, and Wild Rose was not capable of the complex murder involving chloroform and tying up the victim.

supporting_points: He was seen entering and leaving the apartment by witnesses
He fled by the fire escape to avoid suspicion
His glove was found at the crime scene
He had a motive of family resentment
false_solution.the_one_flaw: He was not capable of the murder and was protecting Wild Rose and Esther; evidence later proved his innocence.

red_herrings.description: Cass Hull was suspected due to his threats and presence at the crime scene, and his wife’s aggressive behavior.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Hull was involved in a quarrel but did not commit the murder; he was scared and tried to flee.

red_herrings.description: James Cunningham, Jr.'s secret marriage to Phyllis Harriman and his motive to inherit the fortune made him a prime suspect.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Though guilty of deception and conspiracy, he did not physically commit the murder; the valet Shibo was the actual killer.

closed_circle.rationale: All these individuals had access to the apartment and motives related to the victim; the investigation focused on them exclusively.

discriminating_test.design: Reconstruct the timeline of arrivals and departures at the apartment using witness testimonies and physical evidence such as glove presence, time on watches, and presence on fire escape. Verify the presence of suspects in the apartment during the critical murder window and check for contradictions in alibis and testimonies.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This test reveals who had the opportunity to commit the murder within the narrow time window and who was lying about their presence or actions.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The suspect must be proven to have been present in the apartment during the murder time window with no credible alibi and with access to the murder method.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed timelines, witness testimonies, and physical evidence such as the glove, the note, and the Japanese confession. The presence and movements of all suspects are described, including their motives and alibis. The false solution accusing Kirby Lane is presented and refuted, allowing the reader to deduce the real culprit by careful analysis of the timeline and motives.
